Skunk Ape line: 82 reviews on manufacturer website (C2 version) 138. Shines with amazing grip, epic pop, and its ability to handle uneven snow really well 139. Uneven snow: truly shines; blasts through chunder and uneven terrain like a tank 140. Edge hold: East Coast and ice specialist; tremendous grip and edge hold unbeatable on firm conditions 141. Turning: quick edge to edge; 8.6m sidecut radius offers a balanced turning experience 142. Base glide: "thirsty base" — takes a lot of waxing to keep optimal glide 143. Overall summary: Damp, stiff, aggressive, poppy, and an absolute carving beast 145. carving_rating_tgr: Carving: Great; Uneven Snow: Great; Jumps: Great; Edge Hold: Icy Snow; Speed: Good; Switch: Good; Pipe: Good; Powder: Average; Base Glide: Average; Jibbing: Poor [14] 146. on_snow_feel_tgr: Locked In [14] 147. turn_initiation_performance: Medium [14] 148. reviewer_opinion_the_good_ride: Semi-Hard [14] 149. reviewer_opinion_the_good_ride: Moderate [14] 150. board_weight_grams: Feels Heavy [14] 151. setback: -12.5mm [14] 152. Reviewer fit: 6'3.5", 250 pounds, size 12 boot on 165W — fit perfectly 153. The camber version has a classic "lively" feel underfoot; tester absolutely loved the pop for sidehits 154. Traditional camber had a more consistent feel for turning and was more responsive and poppy for in-bounds riding 155. Traditional camber is less forgiving of mistakes 156. The camber version naturally leans more towards freestyle & fast resort ripping 157. Carving was really fun — camber and Magne-Traction really locks in, making carves effortless 158. Playful side shines in the park; surprisingly poppy for its size, popping ollies and butters with ease 159. The wider platform provides stability at high speeds and the rockered nose helps initiate turns smoothly 160. Base requires frequent waxing to maintain glide — "thirsty base" 161. Can be technical and a little catchy due to the full camber 162. Traditional camber is less forgiving of mistakes — not ideal for beginners 163. Jibbing rated "Poor" by The Good Ride [14] 164. Historical durability concern (older HP model): forum user reported top sheet damage and core snap at nose [26] — Note: this is from a 2013 forum post about an older HP construction model, may not be relevant to current construction. 165. Forum user noted UHMW tip/tail (no steel edge at extremities) leads to top sheet splits and cracks at tips 166. Some riders find the board too stiff for jumps and spins 167. Lib Tech boards have texture on the base requiring frequent waxing; when waxed properly they glide as well as others 168. Mervin produces zero hazardous waste; makes boards in Sequim, WA using eco materials, processes and power 169. Mervin uses the safest epoxy resin systems available, with minimal VOCs 170. No solvents in factory — citrus-based cleaners used instead 171. All electricity used by factory is "green" power contracted from local PUD 172. Mervin uses only renewable forest products for cores 173. FSC-certified Aspen and Paulownia core blend for sustainable construction 174. rider_level: Intermediate–Advanced (merchant) [MERCHANT] 175. skill_level_recommendation: Intermediate–Expert [14] 176. Built for larger, advanced to expert riders who want serious power and float 177. Not just a big version of another board — specially designed for big guys with big boots (smallest waist width 26.8cm) 178. Burton Custom X Wide: flex 6-9/10, traditional camber, sintered WFO base — high-end competitor for advanced big riders 179. Other boards mentioned by big rider community: Never Summer Protosynthesis, Salomon HPS, Bataleon Party Wave Plus, Telos Backslash 180. K2 Party Platter 157 and Ride Superpig 158 also mentioned as wide alternatives for big riders 181. The 2024 Lib Tech Skunk Ape II is one of the best wide snowboards on the market 182. comparable_board_same_brand: Skunk Ape (C2 rocker profile) — same shape/construction, more forgiving, better powder float [10] 183. Lib Tech Skunk Ape Twin (new for 2027): true twin version, less aggressive, more forgiving and playful than directional Skunk Apes 184. Gnu Rider's Choice 166W (waist 268mm) mentioned as comparable by forum riders with size 14/15 boots 185. construction_material_innovation: Floaty ATV nose shape — longer, more relaxed nose for powder float [7][MERCHANT] 186. Tip/tail have been slimmed down to make rotations easier 187. Magne-Traction serrated edge technology bites into hard pack and variable snow where a standard edge loses grip 188. Directional twin shape pairs a floaty ATV nose for pow days with centralized camber that delivers precision, pop, and aggressive response 189. Built in ultra-light HP construction for easy on the front foot chair rides 190. A combo of Bi-Ax and Tri-Ax fiberglass gives this board a solid flex that feels consistent underfoot 191. The Good Ride YouTube review title states "No Changes For 2026" (comparing 2025 to 2026) [34] 192. For the 2027 season, the Skunk Ape Camber continues to be refined by Lib Tech's experiMENTAL Division team riders 193. availability_status: Preorder [MERCHANT]
